_comment: Real, pinned, MIT-licensed Next.js app-router applications vendored as a diffpack acceptance corpus. Source is committed (small); node_modules is NOT (see .gitignore). Each app is verified hermetic: no request-time network, DB, or secrets. Built with `diffpack build-app <app> production`, served by scripts/rsc/next-server.mjs, and curl-smoked by scripts/rsc/next-real-check.sh. Both vendored apps BUILD + SERVE under diffpack (see each `frontier`); a future app that fails is a recorded frontier, never a silent drop.

upstream.note: Vercel's own canonical examples are the reference definition of a real app-router app and are MIT-licensed / redistributable. Each vendored app carries a copy of the upstream LICENSE.

apps.name: hello-world
apps.why: Smallest possible real app-router app: a single RootLayout + a single page. The minimal proof that diffpack recognizes and builds the app/ convention at all.

frontier.notes: Builds all three RSC graphs + prerenders + serves 200 under real diffpack.

apps.name: mdx
apps.why: A richer but still fully hermetic app-router app: static metadata export, next/font/google (Inter), next/image (static svg), CSS Modules, and MDX-at-build (@next/mdx). Exercises several build-time app-router features at once with no request-time data.

smoke.expectBody: This is an example blog page with MDX support

frontier.notes: Builds all three RSC graphs + prerenders + serves 200 under real diffpack. Uses @next/mdx: diffpack ignores the plugin config (best-effort eval) and handles page.mdx natively; custom `mdx-components.tsx` element overrides are NOT wired into diffpack's native MDX (a documented gap, non-blocking).
